# The speed factor is m/s of PCM_SPEED lead per m/s2 of requested accel; the servo's dv gain
# was identified at 0.33-0.46 (m/s2)/(m/s) on the MDX (speedfactor 2.2-3.0), and a gain above
# 1 (m/s2)/(m/s), i.e. a factor below 1.0, is not a plausible comfort-tuned ACC servo.
patch_head_lines: +# Speed-channel learner backstops. These are plant-plausibility bounds, not tuning: a persisted
+# value outside them is a poisoned learner state, not something a Nidec PCM can have taught us.
+# The speed factor is m/s of PCM_SPEED lead per m/s2 of requested accel; the servo's dv gain
+# was identified at 0.33-0.46 (m/s2)/(m/s) on the MDX (speedfactor 2.2-3.0), and a gain above
+# 1 (m/s2)/(m/s), i.e. a factor below 1.0, is not a plausible comfort-tuned ACC servo.
+# zero-accel servo offset, m/s; measured -0.18..+0.46 per speed band on the MDX
+# speed-channel ceiling, m/s2; every Nidec PCM sustains at least this on its speed channel
+# (stock ramps run +0.5..0.8 m/s2), so a lower value is a collapsed learner, not a measurement

+# stock itself launches with a 2.8 m/s lead and the MDX's linear band extends to ~2.5 m/s, so

records.subject: Honda interceptor: drop longitudinal ki from the Nidec servo tune to 0.3
actual_added_code_examples: # The old [1.2, 0.8, 0.5] is the Nidec PCM speed-servo tune. The interceptor is a different
# plant: the plan accel goes straight onto the pedal through a 0.2 pedal/s rise limit, and the
# pedal -> accel response lags 0.5-1 s (longer across a DCT downshift). An integrator at 0.7-1.2
# on that loop winds up through the whole lag: ACURA_ILX route 2752303cce1f0aba|00000000, every
# tip-in ran the integral term to +0.5..+0.7 m/s2 on top of a 1.0-1.3 plan (25-70% of the peak
# pedal), which is what pulled the DCT down two gears, and the overshoot that followed ran it to
# -0.2..-0.3, which is what put the brake on against a -0.1..-0.2 plan. With ~1 s of effective
# loop delay, ki * delay must stay well under 1; 0.3 keeps the term within +-0.2 in replay.
